name: Peripapillary Staphyloma
aliases: Peripapillary Staphyloma of the Optic Nerve

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Imaging Diagnostic Criteria for Peripapillary Staphyloma

criteria.description: Presence of a deep excavation or outpouching around the optic disc observed clinically or on imaging
Relatively normal retinal vessels passing over the staphylomatous excavation without significant displacement
No evidence of glaucomatous optic neuropathy or elevated intraocular pressure
Variable visual acuity often reduced but not necessarily correlated with staphyloma size
Confirmation of peripapillary excavation by ocular imaging modalities such as OCT or B-scan ultrasonography

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of optic disc excavation with normal retinal vessels and imaging confirmation of peripapillary staphyloma without glaucomatous changes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; differentiation from other optic nerve anomalies is essential.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic deep outpouching adjacent to the optic disc

pathognomonic.symptomName: Optic disc enlargement with normal retinal vessel pattern
searchTerms: enlarged optic nerve head with normal vessels
big optic disc without vessel changes
optic disc swelling with normal blood vessels

common.notes: Variable severity depending on staphyloma extent
Often corresponding to the area of excavation

rare.notes: Rarely associated but important to exclude

imaging: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) showing peripapillary scleral excavation
B-scan ultrasonography demonstrating optic disc excavation
Fundus photography revealing enlarged optic disc with excavation
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic optic nerve head morphology

distinguishingFeatures: Coloboma typically involves inferior optic disc margin
More irregular excavation compared to smooth staphyloma
Central glial tuft in optic disc
Radial retinal vessels emerging from disc margin
Funnel-shaped excavation distinct from peripapillary staphyloma

redFlags: Sudden vision loss indicating possible retinal detachment
Elevated intraocular pressure suggesting secondary glaucoma
Rapid progression of visual field defects
references: Duke-Elder S. System of Ophthalmology. Vol. 4. The Anatomy of the Visual System. 1964.
Yanoff M, Duker JS. Ophthalmology. 6th Edition. Elsevier; 2020.
